text.p: The Lighthouse at Gull's End is a short scenario for three or four player characters, for Fate Core or Fate Accelerated (one session, two or three hours). It was written for Kraken VTT; its rules are Fate's.

What you need: the Fate Core System or Fate Accelerated Edition book made active (the character wizard reads it), and this scenario. The Fate Toolkit and Adversaries book has more opposition if the table wants it.

Pregenerated characters: Rook Tallow, Ilsa Fenwright and Corin Gale, each made twice: for Fate Core (skills) and for Fate Accelerated (approaches). In the Characters window a player takes one as it is (Pregenerated), or makes their own with the wizard.

In Kraken: put the game aspects and each scene's situation aspects on the Scene Aspects strip (the GM's + on the strip, or Start a scene: the GM's fate points are set to one a player character). The two conflicts are encounters (drag them onto the combat tracker); the two maps have their zones outlined in colour.

For three nights the great lamp of Gull's End has stayed dark. On the third, the merchant ship Kittiwake broke on the rocks below it, and by morning there was nothing on the beach but planks: her cargo was gone before the tide was.
The harbour town of Saltreach wants to know why the light is out, and the keeper, Isolde Varr, has not come down the cliff in a week.

What is really going on: Captain Mercy Sloane, a smuggler, paid the keeper to let the light go dark, and holds the keeper's son aboard her ship to keep her quiet. Sloane's wreckers, led by Tam Coller (the Lamp-Snuffer), light false fires on the strand to lure ships onto the rocks, and strip what washes in.
Game aspects (on the strip for the whole session, kind game):
Story questions: Will the heroes put the light back before another ship breaks? Will they free Isolde's son? Will Mercy Sloane get away with the Kittiwake's cargo?
The harbour town at dusk. Fishing boats pulled high, a crowd at the harbourmaster's door, and the Kittiwake's widowed owner, Maren Hask, shouting for someone to do something.
Situation aspects: Angry Crowd on the Quay, Fog Rolling In.
What the heroes can learn (overcome or create an advantage against Fair (+2), Contacts, Rapport, Investigate, Empathy; FAE Clever, Flashy, Careful):

list.li: Lights were seen on the strand the night the Kittiwake sank: not the lighthouse's, low and moving. A success makes the aspect False Fires on the Strand (one free invoke).
Tam Coller has been spending silver in the taverns: Tam Coller Is Flush With Silver.
A black-sailed ship has been anchored in the lee of the point: The Ship Without a Flag.

text.p: Compel to offer: a character with a past in Saltreach (Rook's Saltreach Knows My Face) is recognised and held up by old grievances: a fate point if they let it happen.

The way down to the strand and up to the lighthouse is a goat-path along the cliff, at night, in a rising gale. Play it as a challenge: three overcome actions, each by a different hero or skill, against Fair (+2):

list.li: Keep your footing on the wet stone (Athletics; FAE Careful or Quick).
Spot the wreckers' lookout before he sees you (Notice; FAE Careful or Sneaky).
Find the way down in the dark (Lore or Investigate; FAE Clever).

text.p: Situation aspects: Slick Rocks, Howling Gale.

Failures do not stop them: each costs something (a stress box, a lookout who runs to warn Tam Coller, the wreckers ready for them: one free invoke on Ambush in the Dunes for the opposition in Scene Three).

e04scenethreewreckersonthestrand.name: 04 Scene Three: Wreckers on the Strand

text.p: The Strand at Gull's End (the map). The wreckers have built a fire on the beach to draw the next ship in. Tam Coller and three wreckers are stripping the Kittiwake's last crates.
Zones (their outlines on the map):

list.li: Blue: The Surf. Waist-deep, freezing water. Breaking Waves: moving into or out of it is an overcome (Athletics, Fair).
Orange: The Wreck. What is left of the Kittiwake's hull. Splintered Timbers; good cover.
Teal: The Tidepools. Slippery Rock Pools.
Red: The Strand. Open sand, the wreckers' False Beacon Fire burning.
Purple: The Cliff Path. Up to the lighthouse. Narrow Ledge.

text.p: The conflict (the encounter Wreckers on the Strand): Tam Coller (supporting NPC) and Wreckers (nameless, Fair; three, or a mob). The wreckers fight to keep their haul; Tam concedes when the fight turns ("I'll tell you who paid us!") rather than be taken out.

If the heroes put out the false fire (overcome against Good (+3), or as part of an attack's narration on a success with style) another ship is saved: tell the players, and remember it at the milestone.

The Lighthouse at Gull's End (the map). Isolde Varr's cottage and the tower. Captain Mercy Sloane is here with two deckhands, collecting her last payment of silver from the keeper and making sure the lamp stays dark.
Zones (their outlines on the map):

list.li: Orange: The Keeper's Cottage. Isolde is here, Bound to a Chair.
Teal: The Tower Floor. The spiral stair up. Barrels of Lamp Oil.
Yellow: The Lamp Room (upstairs, drawn beside the tower). The great lamp, cold. The Great Lens.
Green: The Yard. The path from the cliff. Wind-Bent Grass.
Red: The Cliff's Edge. A Long Fall to the Rocks.

text.p: The conflict (the encounter The Lamp Room): Mercy Sloane (main NPC) and two Sloane's Deckhands (nameless, Average). Sloane prefers talk to a fight, and a fight to losing: if the heroes threaten her, she offers a bargain (the boy for her freedom). She concedes rather than be taken out, and gets away on her ship unless the heroes have cut her off.
Lighting the lamp is an overcome against Great (+4) (Crafts, Lore; FAE Clever or Careful), easier with Isolde's help (+2, or a free invoke on Isolde Knows This Lamp if a hero frees her).
If the light burns again before dawn, the next ship comes safe into Saltreach, and the town owes the heroes: a new game aspect for the next session, Heroes of Saltreach.
If Mercy Sloane got away, she is a main NPC for the next scenario: give her a new aspect, The Heroes of Gull's End Cost Me Everything.

Milestones: at the end of the session, each player character reaches a minor milestone (switch two skills or approaches, rename an aspect, trade a stunt). If the story questions were answered (the light lit, the boy freed), it is a significant milestone instead: a skill point too. In Kraken: the sheet's Milestones tab, or the party sheet's Milestones tab for everyone at once.
Three heroes who know each other already (their aspects say so):

list.li: Rook Tallow, Disgraced Captain of the Harbour Watch: a fighter, stubborn and loyal; trouble I Owe the Wrong People.
Ilsa Fenwright, Weather-Witch of the Western Isles: wise in old lore and the moods of the sea; trouble The Storm Answers Before I Ask.
Corin Gale, Smuggler With a Conscience: a liar and a sailor; trouble Mercy Sloane Wants Me Back (the GM's best compel tonight).
